currentAffairs.title: India’s merchandise exports reach a record in October 2026
currentAffairs.summary: India’s merchandise exports were US$49.47 billion in October 2026, up from US$34.11 billion in October 2025 (about 45.06%). Merchandise imports were US$89.35 billion, producing a merchandise trade deficit of US$39.88 billion. The Ministry estimated combined merchandise-and-services exports at US$89.99 billion and imports at US$110.07 billion, a combined trade deficit of US$20.09 billion. Important caveat: October 2026 services figures are estimates because the latest RBI services data available to the ministry was for September 2026.
currentAffairs.takeaway: Exam link: merchandise trade covers goods; total trade combines goods and services. Do not confuse the US$39.88 billion merchandise deficit with the US$20.09 billion combined deficit.
currentAffairs.source: Ministry of Commerce & Industry / Press Information Bureau, 13 November 2026

currentAffairs.title: DGFT prohibits export of lithium-ion battery black mass
currentAffairs.summary: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), through Notification No. 49/2026-27 dated 10 November 2026, changed the export policy for lithium-ion battery black mass under ITC(HS) code 85491400 from ‘Free’ to ‘Prohibited’, with immediate effect and until further orders. Black mass is the powder produced by shredding end-of-life lithium-ion batteries and battery-manufacturing waste. It contains recoverable critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese. The government says retaining this material in India should provide feedstock to domestic recyclers, improve capacity utilisation and reduce import dependence.
currentAffairs.takeaway: Exam link: connect the export restriction with critical-mineral security, battery recycling, electric vehicles, energy storage and the circular economy. The measure applies until further orders.
currentAffairs.source: Ministry of Commerce & Industry / Press Information Bureau, 11 November 2026

currentAffairs.title: RBI gives Paytm conditional in-principle approval for wallet business
currentAffairs.summary: On 13 November 2026, the Reserve Bank of India granted in-principle authorisation to Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), a wholly owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, to set up and operate a payment system for issuing prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including digital wallets. This is only preliminary approval: PPSL cannot begin wallet operations until it receives final authorisation (a Certificate of Authorisation). The RBI has also required a system audit, including cybersecurity checks, and submission of the audit report within six months of its letter. PPSL is distinct from Paytm Payments Bank, whose banking licence was cancelled earlier in 2026.
currentAffairs.takeaway: Exam link: understand prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), digital wallets and the RBI’s role in regulating payment systems. Do not describe the in-principle approval as permission to launch immediately.
currentAffairs.source: The Indian Express, 13 November 2026; Reuters, 13 November 2026

currentAffairs.title: IMD tracks a developing low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal
currentAffairs.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported a low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal. Its forecast said the system was likely to become a well-marked low-pressure area on 14 November, develop into a depression around the morning of 15 November, and could intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central Bay of Bengal around the evening of 16 November. These are forecast stages, not confirmation that a cyclone had already formed.
currentAffairs.takeaway: Exam link: know the sequence low-pressure area → well-marked low-pressure area → depression → cyclonic storm. Treat forecast language as probability, not a confirmed event.

vocabulary.meaning: A sudden and large increase; as a verb, to increase suddenly and by a large amount.
vocabulary.example: Merchandise exports recorded a surge in October.

vocabulary.meaning: The amount by which something is less than what is needed, expected or available; in trade, the excess of imports over exports.
vocabulary.example: India recorded a merchandise trade deficit in October.

vocabulary.meaning: To officially forbid something, usually through a law, rule or order.
vocabulary.example: The notification prohibits the export of lithium-ion battery black mass.

vocabulary.meaning: Raw material used in an industrial process to make another product.
vocabulary.example: Domestic recyclers need a reliable supply of black mass as feedstock.

vocabulary.meaning: Able to be obtained, extracted or brought back.
vocabulary.example: Black mass contains recoverable quantities of lithium and cobalt.

vocabulary.meaning: Depending on a particular condition being met.
vocabulary.example: The wallet approval is conditional on receiving final authorisation.
PPSL needs final authorisation before it can start wallet operations.

vocabulary.meaning: The act of obeying a law, rule or official requirement.
vocabulary.example: Payment-system operators must maintain compliance with RBI directions.

vocabulary.meaning: To become stronger or more extreme, or to make something stronger or more extreme.
vocabulary.example: The weather system may intensify over the Bay of Bengal.

vocabulary.meaning: The process of adding different types or varieties of something.
vocabulary.example: Export diversification can reduce reliance on a small number of products or markets.
